output.name: code_interpreter
output.title: code_interpreter
output.description:
Tool for executing Python code.
You will provide the code to be interpreted and executed. This is useful for tasks that require dynamic code generation
and execution, such as data processing, mathematical computations, or any other operations that you cannot perform directly.
When you send Python code to `python` tool, it runs in a **stateful Jupyter notebook environment**.  
The execution will return results or **time out after 90 seconds** if it exceeds the allowed runtime.  
- The `/mnt/data` drive can be used to **save and persist user files**.  
- **Internet access is disabled**, meaning external web requests and API calls **will fail**—avoid making them.

code.description:
The Python code to execute in the sandboxed container.
                    The code should be valid Python syntax and can include imports, file operations,
                    data processing, calculations, and visualizations.

file_ids.description:
List of file IDs to make available in the code execution environment.
                    These files can be referenced and used by the Python code.

items.description: File ID to include in the container

memory_limit.description:
Optional memory limit for the code interpreter container (e.g. '1g', '4g', '16g', '64g').
                    If not provided, the container default memory limit is used.

container.description:
Optional ID of an existing code interpreter container to reuse.
                    Cannot be combined with file_ids, memory_limit, or network_policy.

network_policy.description: Optional outbound network access policy for the code interpreter container.

model_info.description: Information about the model to use for code generation from natural language. If not provided, the model from APIM headers will be used.

deployment_name.description: The deployment name of the model.

previous_response_id.description: Optional previous response ID to use for context of this request.

output.name: web_search
output.title: web_search
output.description:
Tool for performing a web search to add context to your responses when user query needs any factual information, statistics, claims or fresh information that is not in your training data.
Use this tool to retrieve relevant web search results based on a user's query.

search_query.description:
The search query to execute.
                    This query will be used to retrieve relevant web search results.
                    It should be a well-formed string that accurately represents the user's intent.

previous_response_id.description: Optional previous response ID to use for context of this request.

user_location.description: Optional approximate user location to bias web search results.

region.description: Region/state to bias search results towards.

city.description: City to bias search results towards.

filters.description: Optional domain filters for web search results.

search_context_size.description: How much context to retrieve and include from web search results.

model_info.description: Information about the model to be used for web search. If not provided, the model from APIM headers will be used.

deployment_name.description: The deployment name of the model.
